payload.vision_scope_stated: Complete across M1: vision INHERITS se.vision + the delta (default isolation, proven-live, local trimmable machine); as-is = 3 pains (isolation shipped off, live path never run, no local top-level machine) with witnesses; RAID open; frame = gap-claim + why-now + value-props with pass lines; scope = default provisioning + live routing + local machines + live-test acceptance (+ folded owner feedback: trim=skip and the inherit-se.vision guidance fix); non-goals = general strike-list, deviation-judgment automation, the porting/red-team audit, the two-at-once demo, phone, i9 tabs.
payload.problem_agreed: The delta is real and witnessed this session: i5's worktree lane is opt-in with no iteration setting the flag (plan.json), so isolation shipped effectively OFF, and its live path was never run (unit tests hand-root the loop). Both are logged defects (note-e8a12b600638, note-6815f9db4930). The goal is worth having because isolation was the blessed i5 promise, and because unattended/parallel work is unsafe without real per-iteration isolation and an honest merge - and because 'shipped but never run for real' is a regression we must close, not repeat.
payload.prior_art_positioned: Against the field: raw git worktrees give isolation without process (no auto merge/suspect, no local machine); i5's own lane built the primitives but shipped opt-in and unproven; parallel agent sessions give throughput without honest merge; a shared-template machine gives one process for all with no local trim. None keeps default-isolation + proven-live + local-trim + honest-suspect-merge together. i5b completes its direct predecessor (i5) rather than inventing anew.
